reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a highly regular, near-periodic pulse train with a fundamental period of approximately 96 points (matching the estimated period). Each cycle consists of a sharp, near-vertical rise from baseline (≈0.0) to a peak between 1.5–3.3 robust-standardized units, followed by a rapid drop back to baseline within 1–2 points. Peaks are narrow (1–2 points wide), symmetric or slightly right-skewed, and exhibit minimal intra-peak variability. Between pulses, the signal remains flat at baseline (0.0) with negligible noise—roughness metrics near zero confirm this. Amplitude is stable across cycles: 90th-percentile amplitude ranges narrowly from 2.41 to 2.47, and upper extremes cluster at ~2.86 or ~3.31, suggesting two common peak-height modes. Minor morphological variation exists: some pulses show small pre-peak shoulders or post-peak plateaus (e.g., candidate 0 at index ~12–15), but these are consistent across candidates and likely part of the nominal shape. No sustained trend is present; slope_per_point values are near zero (≤|0.018|), and curvature varies due to pulse density and local morphology, not underlying drift. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates begin/end mid-cycle but preserve full pulse shapes internally. Acceptable variation includes: (1) occasional double-peaked or slightly broader pulses (≤3 points), (2) minor baseline jitter (<0.1), (3) two amplitude regimes (~2.86 vs ~3.31 peaks), likely reflecting natural modulation rather than anomaly.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 1 for queries with tight, symmetric pulses and minimal variation; use candidate 3 when query spans >300 points or shows slight downward drift; candidate 2 is optimal for queries exhibiting mild shoulder features or moderate roughness; avoid candidate 0 unless query matches its early-ramp morphology exactly—it is the least reliable due to the anomalous plateau. For amplitude-matching, treat ~2.86 and ~3.31 as equally valid normal modes.
uncertainties: Exact cause of bimodal peak heights (2.86 vs 3.31) is unknown—could be intrinsic modulation or sensor quantization
Whether the early plateau in candidate 0 is a rare normal variant or low-level contamination cannot be resolved without labels
Robust standardization used median/MAD; absolute scale is lost, so amplitude interpretation is relative only
No ground-truth confirms whether the slight negative slope in candidate 3 is systematic or incidental
